# Decisions: record-graph

- 2026-08-03T10:28:25.921Z — chose **A mechanical graph derived only from facts already present in the event logs (envelope.session, file_touched, command_run, task_status_changed, decision_logged, plan structure, bindings)** over A semantic/knowledge graph in the graphify sense — LLM entity+relation extraction, embeddings, community detection over record prose because Semantic extraction requires inference, which violates the zero-model-API-call invariant (SPEC §Architectural invariants) and is the felt-cost D3 rejection verbatim. The edges are already typed facts in the log; the per-initiative fold simply flattens them and drops every cross-initiative one. Deriving them costs nothing and stays retroactive over all existing records.
- 2026-08-03T10:28:28.893Z — chose **Explicit CLI surface (`sofar why`, `sofar related`) as the only consumer of buildGraph, enforced by a hot-path exclusion test** over Feeding graph results into the SessionStart block, get_state digest, or UserPromptSubmit shim because buildGraph reads N event logs where the fold reads one, so it cannot fit the 100ms shim budget (speed T2) — wiring it into the injected context would regress exactly the latency speed-2 is buying back. Pull, not push: the queries answer questions a human or agent asks deliberately.
- 2026-08-03T10:45:25.471Z — chose **Derive repo-generality from citation behaviour — a decision cited from initiatives other than its own is repo-general — via a mechanical `cites` edge over the stable handle grammar (D&lt;n&gt;, BD&lt;n&gt;, &lt;slug&gt; D&lt;n&gt;, speed T&lt;n&gt;)** over Adding a declared `scope: repo|initiative` field to the decision_logged payload, with a doctor check over it because A scope field would be the first derivation in this engine that is NOT retroactive — task_files, freshness and unregistered_sessions are each specified as covering every existing record. 136 decisions already exist with no scope, so D3 itself would be invisible to the check built to protect D3, and closing that needs hand-classification of the back catalogue. Scope also demands a judgment unavailable at log time (decisions BECOME repo-general later) and fails silently when under-scoped. Citation handles are already in the record: 150 citations across 12 initiatives, measured 2026-08-03. Deriving costs no schema change, no new capture, no judgment, and covers all 136 retroactively. Revisit scope only if the derived signal proves noisy in practice.
- 2026-08-03T14:19:33.480Z — chose **Three node families with distinct identity rules — STRUCTURAL (initiative/phase/task, from each initiative's final folded plan, slug-scoped because task ids like "1.1" repeat across most initiatives), OCCURRENCE (command/decision/note, one node per sourcing event keyed by its ulid), JOIN (session/file, deliberately NOT slug-scoped) — and occurrence EDGES kept as multi-edges, one per sourcing event, never deduped into pairs.** over A flat node table with deduped (from,to) pairs and a count attribute, which is the conventional adjacency shape and about half the memory. because The join nodes ARE the cross-initiative edge: a session id and a repo-relative path mean the same thing in every log that mentions them, so not scoping them is what recovers the provenance the per-initiative fold structurally drops. And deduping occurrence edges would make Phase 4 impossible — activity's task_changes renders EVERY status change in log order including repeats on one task, and its files list is first-touch-ordered, so a pair-deduped edge set cannot reproduce it byte-identically. Since 4.1/4.2 byte-identity is the GO/NO-GO for the whole initiative, the primitive has to keep per-event grain and let each query dedupe on the read side.
- 2026-08-03T14:19:45.295Z — chose **Tighten the citation grammar against measurement: bare &lt;n&gt;.&lt;n&gt; is NOT a handle (needs its slug), BD&lt;n&gt; and D-&lt;label&gt; are recorded as dangling rather than resolved, D&lt;n&gt; resolves to the nth decision_logged in that initiative's log in ulid order, and self-citations plus targets sorting AFTER the citing decision are dropped. Unresolved handles are carried on the citing decision node as dangling[], never silently discarded.** over The plan's looser sketch — D&lt;n&gt;, BD&lt;n&gt;, &lt;slug&gt; D&lt;n&gt;, speed T&lt;n&gt; matched literally, which is what produced the "150 citations across 12 initiatives" figure the initiative was scoped on. because Measured on the live record, the loose grammar yields 275 tokens of which most are junk: bare &lt;n&gt;.&lt;n&gt; matches version strings (0.1, 0.7, 0.8) and the IP octet 127.0 — 20 false positives and zero true ones. Tightened, 62 tokens resolve to 22 decision edges and 11 task edges with 19 dangling. BD&lt;n&gt; (the most-cited family, BD22/BD16/BD9 at 7x each) names the archived pre-migration prose record in docs/harness.md, which has no nodes here — resolving it would require inference, and D3 forbids that; recording it keeps the signal without inventing an edge. The ordinal rule is not invented for the graph: felt-cost D3 round-trips to the zero-model-API-calls decision that SPEC cites by that handle, and repoGeneral's top result on this repo is that same decision, cited from record-graph and sync-client.
- 2026-08-03T14:48:32.885Z — chose **Graph queries cap at GRAPH_RESULT_CAP (20, the task_files/activity number) and report the overflow as a NUMERIC `omitted` field alongside the typed list. The "+N more" string stays a render-time concern, emitted by the CLI surfaces in 3.1/3.2.** over 2.4 as written — mirroring activity's precedent literally by appending a "+N more" STRING into the result arrays themselves. because The in-band sentinel is already a proven wart in this codebase: because activity.files can end in "+N more", openSessionFileConflicts has to defend with `if (file.startsWith('+')) continue` (fold.ts) — a fake element in a typed list that every downstream consumer must remember is not a file. Query results are typed structures consumed by renderers and by doctor (3.3), so repeating that would spread the defensive check further. Same cap, same user-visible "+N more" text, no poisoned arrays. Ordering and dedupe DO follow the task_files precedent unchanged: dedupe most-recent-first, newest-first output.
- 2026-08-03T14:52:01.277Z — chose **Keep recorded file paths VERBATIM as node identity and resolve a queried path at read time: exact hit wins, otherwise every recorded path ending at a segment boundary with the query matches, and the caller reports matched_paths. relatedTasks keeps joining on exact recorded identity.** over Canonicalizing paths at build time — stripping the repo root and any leading .claude/worktrees/&lt;name&gt;/ so each logical file gets one node. because file_touched records ABSOLUTE paths, so one logical file accumulates an identity per checkout it was ever edited from. Measured: 229 file nodes, 89 outside the current root, 38 worktree-prefixed, 21 paths split across checkouts — packages/engine/src/cli/doctor.ts exists under four. No prefix rule recovers the biggest split, because /Users/jins/IO/harness is the PRE-RENAME root of this same repo (harness to sofar, Jul 7) and nothing mechanical connects the two directory names; canonicalizing would fix worktrees and miss the rename while quietly rewriting what the record says. Suffix resolution catches all of them, stays literal, and lets the caller pick specificity. Confirmed on the live record: whyFile for packages/engine/src/core/fold.ts goes from 5 sessions across 4 initiatives to 7 across 6. relatedTasks is left exact because widening it means choosing a canonical suffix length for every path, which is a guess — under-reporting a neighbour is the safer error.
